where: calc.js · rrDmg, D3 A/S, granted ANTI-X, granted INDIRECT FIRE
why: Hand-worked, all right: rrDmg D6 S8 TORRENT vs T4 big model, 50 wounds × (½·3.5 + ½·5) = 212.5; rrDmg D3 50 × 7/3; +D3 S on S3 vs T4: 60 × (½ + ⅔ + ⅔)/3 = 36.67; +D3 A: 10 × 3 = 30; granted ANTI-VEHICLE 4+ with assume and [DEVASTATING WOUNDS], S4 vs T8 (normally 6+): 30 mortals of 60; granted [INDIRECT FIRE] with indirect 1-5: 10 of 60 hit (without the grant indirect does nothing, 30). The fx: calc-test expectations are right, and the old engine cases are unchanged (the 13 cases removed are all Damage-tab cases tied to old readings or ticked-for-you; none is an engine case). Averages are right. Three code fixes: (1) 'once per batch' is not what the Core Rules say. 02.02.03 Random Attacks: 'If several weapons with random A characteristics are making identical attacks, generate the attacks for each of those weapons individually'. Other Random Characteristics (S): 'roll … on an individual, per-model or per-weapon basis each time that characteristic is required'. attackOnce rolls one aRoll/sRoll for the whole batch, shared by every model in it. Today only Sacrificial Blessing (one Tzaangor Shaman, one weapon) has a D3 A/S effect, so the averages and this case are unaffected, but played-out kill chances are wrong for n>1. The header also says 'rolled once … in each game'. (2) explain dmgCap: for the mortal-wound part capOf uses pd (re-rolled Damage) while dM uses pd0, so it disagrees with itself when rrDmg and [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] are both on. (3) effects.js toMod: when two critHit/critWound values merge, the last one wins instead of the lowest. Minor: nothing combines them today.

why: Re-run independently, main 0ac28e3 against 653bf81 in my own worktrees. I took 66 random list × unit × phase cases and matched boxes by source name and canonical effect only, never by numbers. Every other box was explicitly off, and I used 4 targets (5×T4 Sv3 W2; 10×T3 Sv5 W1; 1×T11 Sv3 W24 InSv5; 3×T6 Sv2 W3 FNP5). Results: nothing ticked, 264/264 identical. where: verify/derive.js · stratNeeds struck TARGET words (and invariants.js, evidence.js, effects.js norm, effects-extract.js)
why: Struck words are not GW's errata. In the cached Wahapedia HTML every one is `<span class="tooltip" title="Keyword does not appear in that faction."><s class="kwbs">…</s>`: Vox-howl's WAR DOG CHARACTER, Impenetrable Bastion's MONSTER, Crazed Rampage's DEFF DREAD, and even 'Bomb SQUIG abilities' and WURRBOY. waha-extract.py:23 turns kwbs into ~~…~~. GW's words are unchanged. derive.js:33-34 itself says so ('Struck words are kept: Wahapedia strikes a keyword that does not appear in the faction'), and so does the data.js:1208 comment on Vox-howl. Consequences: (a) Vox-howl lost its needs, so every unit of the list meets it. In woof-woof, War Dog Brigand, Executioner and Karnivore were not eligible on main and are now listed under Stratagems. This is a REGRESSION, missing from changes.md. (b) Impenetrable Bastion needs none:['Vehicle'], having lost 'Monster'. No unit changes today (Custodes have no MONSTER), but it is not GW's TARGET. (c) Daemonic Infestation, none:['Pink Horrors'] → unless:{all:['Pink','Horrors']}: unrelated to striking, and a correction (the lists keep the keyword as two words, so main's none never matched). No list has Pink Horrors, so nothing changes today. (d) effects.js norm and effects-extract plainCase/targetKw drop struck words from every rule sentence too, which can widen a reach or target condition.
fix: Keep struck words and drop only the markers: verify/derive.js:608-609 `const target = norm(s.target), when = …` (norm already strips ~~); verify/invariants.js:56,59 drop `.replace(/~~[^~]*~~\s*\/?\s*/g, '')`; verify/evidence.js:129 `let t = String(s.target).replace(/~~/g, '')…`; effects.js:133 and verify/effects-extract.js:24 replace `~~[^~]*~~` with `~~` in the regex; verify/effects-extract.js:66 `Dv.prepBold(s.replace(/~~/g, ''))`. data.js:1210 Vox-howl back to `needs:{ all:['War Dog','Character'] }` (main's); data.js:1321 Impenetrable Bastion `needs:{ all:['Faction: Adeptus Custodes'], none:['Monster','Vehicle'] }`; then node verify/effects-migrate.js --write (the norm change can move BOXES).

why: I broke things on purpose in a scratch worktree, then restored it. Not caught: (1) the extractor writing a hand `note:'…'` onto a box, then --write. The gate passes, because G1-G7 have no box schema, so free-text hand fields can sit in BOXES. (2) a Unit-rules box made to appear only when `(au.mods||[]).some(m => m.from === ab.name)`. (3) an other-units box made to depend on `x.mods`. G6 only greps m.note/m.when/m.calc/calcMods, and there is no sources check for the army/unit/other groups as there is for stratagems. (4) G6 scans only app.html between '/* ---------- screen: damage' and 'function screenDamage(', so the drawing code (screenDamage, :3253-3852) is not scanned. It is clean today. (5) G1-G5 run on M.build(D), not data.js; that is fine because G7 ties them together. Remaining reading columns the tab uses: ab.damaged (tables.js READ_COLS.ability, a copy of the 'Damaged: 1-N' name, app.html:2157 and dmCalc) and ab.embarked (a hand reading, dmEmbarked, Sir Hekhtur), carried over from main.

why: No rule prose is parsed at run time. The only regex tests are ab.tag (GW's (Aura) tag), weapon keywords and app-made strings; there is no dmEffects or extractor, and effects and conditions come from BOXES as data. Every box starts unticked, except when the player sets a fact of the table. The five groups and the strat-on-other-unit routing are right. One latent bug in dmBaked: for a keyword effect it tests `keys.some(k => k.startsWith(l) || l.startsWith(k))` over all of the weapon's from-keys, including the stats A/S/D/AP/WS. So a rule that printed +S into a weapon would also 'bake' its [SUSTAINED HITS …] ('SUSTAINED HITS 1'.startsWith('S')), and likewise D vs [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] and A vs [ANTI-…]. No list hits it today (I checked every weapon's from against its rule's boxes).
fix: app.html:2146-2147: `const kws = keys.filter(k => !/^(?:A|S|D|AP|WS|BS)$/.test(k)); return !!l && kws.some(k => k.startsWith(l) || l.startsWith(k));`
